svg.text: The watermark generator — why max() is load-bearing
naive formula regresses 2x (−40s, −170s) · correct formula never does
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed · key = which SOURCE it came from
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the straggler
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the assumed worst-case skew, in seconds. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: W0 — the window this chapter follows. W0 = 0 ([12:00, 12:02))
12 // primitive: KEYS — the source names. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
13 // primitive: max(xs) — the largest element. max([1, 3, 2]) = 3
14 // primitive: min(xs) — the smallest element. min([1, 3, 2]) = 1
15 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the WIN-second window holding et.
17 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those event ids.
19 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
23 // function: naiveWatermark(e) — THE BUG: this event's own time, minus LAG.
29 // function: correctWatermark(seen, e) — the max so far, then minus LAG.
33 if (m == NONE || e.et > m) { m = e.et }
37 // function: run(useMax) — generate a watermark per event, counting any value
38 // that is lower than the one before it.
46 if (seen == NONE || e.et > seen) { seen = e.et }
49 if (prev != NONE && w < prev) { back = back + 1 }
56 // primitive: windowStarts() — every window start in this stream. windowStarts() = [0, 120, 240, 480]
58 // function: reopened(g) — windows a regression would UN-close: already past the
59 // watermark once, and below it again afterwards.
67 if (g.emitted[j] < w + WIN) { out = append(out, w) }
75 // function: main() — THE CALLER: both formulas, same stream.
Step 3/0 — one line makes it monotonic
Same event, and `m` stays at 260 because `e.et` (220) is not greater. The emitted value is 200 — equal to the previous one, never below it. `back` stays 0 for the whole
stream: 2 regressions become 0 by replacing `e.et` with `max(seen, e.et)`.
